contracts.objects: General V subsetR^d, predictions x_t inV, arbitrary real loss functions ell_t:V->R, fixed comparator u inV.
contracts.formula: Regret_T(u)=sum_{t=1}^T ell_t(x_t)-sum_{t=1}^T ell_t(u). Squared-game empirical-best variant: R*_T=sum(x_t-y_t)^2-min_{u in[0,1]}sum(u-y_t)^2.
contracts.quantifiers: For every finite positive horizon and admissible data/loss/prediction sequence; u fixed across rounds. Empirical-best u*_T may depend on the entire horizon/path.
contracts.probability: General definition deterministic, no probability mode specified. P2 opening expected-fixed version has min outside expectation.
contracts.boundary: Fixed-u regret and empirical-best regret are not identical; the latter is maximum over fixed-u regrets at a given horizon. No automatic nonnegativity for arbitrary algorithms.

contracts.kind: printed definition with unresolved ordinary-limit applicability
contracts.quantifiers: For every fixed u inV. Source ordinary lim notation, not limsup. Algorithm need not know u.
contracts.interpretation: Ordinary limit notation normally presupposes existence. Source does not specify finite versus extended-real limit; in bounded square-loss case normalized regrets lie[-1,1], so any limit is finite.
contracts.boundary: Cannot silently replace with limsup or require zero limit. Source phrase at most sublinear is one-sided; fixed regret may be negative linear. Theorem1.3 alone does not establish ordinary-limit existence for every fixed u.

contracts.signature: For every positive integer T and y_1,...,y_T in[0,1], set x_1=1/2, x_t=(sum_{i<t} y_i)/(t-1) for t>=2. Then R*_T<=4+4 lnT.
premises: T positive integer implicit in log/sums
contracts.conclusion: Finite empirical-best regret upper bound, not a lower bound or fixed-comparator ordinary-limit theorem.
contracts.probability: Pathwise, no IID/probability assumptions; may hold along adaptive adversary realizations.
contracts.boundary: Informal p3 permits arbitrary first prediction; theorem specializes to1/2. Source explicitly leaves minimaxity/lower rate unproved.

contracts.signature: C_T=E sum(x_t-Y_t)^2-T sigma^2; A_T=E sum(x_t-Y_t)^2/T-sigma^2. Success: C_T grows sublinearly iff A_T->0.
premises: Expected losses well defined under bounded prediction convention
contracts.quantifiers: One strategy/process as horizon tends infinity, source criterion not assertion of universal success.
contracts.boundary: Different from deterministic R*_T and fixed R_T(u). No source permission to identify all three metrics; stochastic application requires benchmark and causal bridges.

contracts.signature: m_T=(1/T)sum y_t is empirical squared-loss minimizer in[0,1].
x_t=m_{t-1} for t>=2, x_1=1/2 in Theorem1.3.
contracts.boundary: Strictly past, not mean including current observation.

contracts.signature: For arbitrary losses ell_t:V->R and prefix minimizers x*_t in argmin_V sum_{i<=t}ell_i, sum_t ell_t(x*_t)<=sum_t ell_t(x*_T).
premises: Each relevant prefix minimum attained inV
contracts.boundary: No convexity/IID assumption; existence premise supplied by empirical mean for square-loss application. Induction hypothesis is not final public premise.
Algebra alone, not a zero-limit or ordinary-limit existence theorem.
